title: KLANDESTINE FIELD MANUAL
subtitle: Know the rules. Hide your allegiance. Never assume the table is telling you the truth.

content.objective: Be the last faction standing, or fulfill your faction's secret victory condition before the others catch on.
content.overview: Kloak & Daggurrs: Klandestine is a game of hidden allegiances, strategic deception, and calculated betrayal. Each player secretly belongs to one of thirteen factions, each with unique abilities and win conditions.

steps: Each player secretly draws 1 faction card and keeps it hidden.
Place the remaining deck in the center.
content.factionSetup: Your faction determines your special ability and your secret win condition. Never reveal your faction unless a card effect forces you to.

content.overview: Each turn consists of three phases:

phases.name: 1. Draw Phase
phases.description: Draw 2 cards from the deck. If the deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile.

phases.name: 2. Action Phase
phases.description: Play up to 2 cards from your hand. Cards can be:
options: Played face-down: Placed as a 'Kloak' — a hidden trap or bluff.

phases.name: 3. End Phase
phases.description: Max hand size is 7. Discard down if needed. Pass turn clockwise.

content.overview: Cards come in different rarities with different power levels:

cardTypes.name: Common Cards
cardTypes.description: Basic actions: Draw, Discard, Block. The foundation of every hand.

cardTypes.name: Uncommon Cards
cardTypes.description: Utility effects: Peek at a Kloak, force a discard, swap hands.

cardTypes.name: Rare Cards
cardTypes.description: Powerful one-time effects: Steal a Kloak, reveal a faction, nullify an action.

cardTypes.name: Mythic Cards
cardTypes.description: Game-changing abilities: Reset the board, force all players to reveal, swap factions.

cardTypes.name: Gold Cards
cardTypes.description: Faction-specific ultimates. Only usable if you control the matching faction. Devastating when played correctly.

content.overview: When a player attacks another, the defender may flip a face-down Kloak card. The Kloak's hidden effect resolves immediately — this could block the attack, redirect it, or trigger a trap.
resolvingKloaks: Defender chooses to flip 0, 1, or 2 Kloaks.
Kloak effects resolve in order played.
If attack still valid, damage is dealt.
content.bluffing: You can play any card face-down as a Kloak — even a Common. The threat is often more powerful than the card itself.

content.overview: K&D cards are designed to be modular. Use them as:

uses.name: Magic: The Gathering — Commander Tokens
uses.description: Gold cards make excellent custom commander representations. Their faction abilities map well to commander color identities.

uses.name: D&D — Spell Cards & NPC Factions
uses.description: Use the thirteen factions as rival guilds in your campaign. Card effects translate directly to encounter abilities.

uses.name: Board Games — Event Deck
uses.description: Shuffle K&D cards into any game's event deck. The rarity system balances randomness.

uses.name: Custom Formats
uses.description: Build your own formats. Some community favorites:
formats: Kloak Only: All cards played face-down. Pure bluffing.
Faction Wars: Players openly play their faction. No secrets.
Solitaire: Survive 20 turns against an automated 'Shadow' deck.
